Chapter 6: The World Shifts and So Do We
Have you ever noticed how world events can suddenly feel like they’re happening right on your doorstep? For this family, the news isn’t just background noise anymore—it’s personal. When tensions rise between Iran and America, their carefully built sense of home starts to feel a little shaky.
The kids are the first to pick up on these changes. There are those sideways glances in the hallway, questions that sting just a bit more than usual, and jokes that aren’t as harmless as they sound.
Picture this: one afternoon at school, a teacher hesitates before calling on a student, unsure how to say her name. The pause stretches out, and suddenly, all eyes are on her. Even though she feels the pressure, she manages a soft smile and gently corrects the teacher. But later, when a friend asks if her family is "like the people on TV," that question lingers—unintended, but it still hurts.
Back at home, the parents do their best to protect their children from the world’s harshness. The father, once eager to discuss world events, now chooses his words more carefully. The mother, who’s always found comfort in daily routines, holds tight to tradition. She lights candles for Nowruz, the Persian New Year, and makes the same dishes her mother did. Around the dinner table, the family shares stories and laughter, determined to keep fear outside their door.
It’s a reminder that when the world shifts, even your safest spaces can feel different. But this family doesn’t let suspicion or misunderstanding define who they are. Instead, they open their doors wider—they invite neighbors over, share their celebrations, and answer questions with patience. What they discover is that most people are just curious—willing to understand, if you give them the chance.
Humor becomes their secret weapon. When the father gets mistaken for someone else at work, he turns the story into a dinner table joke, leaving everyone in stitches. The kids learn to meet awkward questions with grace—and sometimes, even a clever comeback. It’s not always easy, but it’s how they take back a sense of control and show everyone around them that they’re much more than the headlines.
So, what’s the real takeaway here? The world may shift in unexpected ways, but who you are—your identity, your family’s love—can’t be shaken by outside events. It’s built, day by day, in the choices you make and the warmth you share. And no matter what’s happening out there, that sense of self endures.
